hypothesis: When PySnooper's file-output path is used with a non-ASCII trace string, FileWriter.write opens the output file without an explicit encoding, so on a non-UTF-8 locale the write can fail or corrupt the trace instead of preserving the Unicode text.
trigger: Create a temporary output path, decorate a function that assigns a non-ASCII string local variable with @pysnooper.snoop(path), run the function under a non-UTF-8 default text encoding, then read the file back as UTF-8 and assert the non-ASCII value appears.

oracle.expected_behavior: Tracing to a requested filesystem path must write the trace text to that path and preserve non-ASCII variable representations, independent of the process locale.
oracle.target_evidence: pysnooper/tracer.py FileWriter.write opens the path with open(self.path, 'w' if self.overwrite else 'a') and no encoding argument; get_write_function routes string/PathLike output to FileWriter; README documents @pysnooper.snoop('/my/log/file.log') and tests/test_pysnooper.py test_file_output exercises path output.
oracle.historical_evidence: cookiecutter:1 shows locale-dependent implicit text I/O encoding for non-ASCII data; PySnooper:3 shows path-output file writing is a public, tested behavior but does not establish the encoding mechanism.

preconditions: Python 3.9.18 runtime with LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 so the default text encoding is ASCII.
pysnooper is importable from the buggy checkout.

initial_state.named_state: no output file exists at the temporary path

actions.description: Set LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 in the process environment before importing pysnooper.
Create a temporary directory and choose a non-existent output path tmpdir/unicode_trace.log.
Import pysnooper and define a function decorated with @pysnooper.snoop(path) that assigns a local variable to the non-ASCII string 'café'.
Call the decorated function so the tracer writes trace lines containing the repr of the non-ASCII local variable to the path.
Open the output path with encoding='utf-8' and read its full text.

plans.expected_invariant: The trace file written to the requested path contains the non-ASCII value 'café' preserved as Unicode text.

observable.measurement_point: after the decorated function returns and the trace file is closed
observable.extraction_method: read the file at the requested path using open(path, encoding='utf-8') and search for the substring 'café'

assertion.predicate: The UTF-8 decoded trace file contains the exact substring 'café'.
assertion.failure_condition: The substring 'café' is absent, or reading the file as UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError, or the decorated call raised UnicodeEncodeError before writing.
assertion.rationale: If FileWriter.write opens the path without encoding='utf-8' under an ASCII locale, the non-ASCII repr cannot be written correctly, so the exact Unicode value will be missing or the write will fail.

initial_state.named_state: an existing output file at the temporary path contains the ASCII prefix 'lala'

actions.description: Set LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 in the process environment before importing pysnooper.
Create a temporary directory and write an existing file tmpdir/append_trace.log containing the ASCII text 'lala'.
Import pysnooper and define a function decorated with @pysnooper.snoop(path) using the default overwrite=False so FileWriter appends, assigning a local variable to the non-ASCII string 'naïve'.
Call the decorated function so the tracer appends trace lines containing the repr of the non-ASCII local variable to the existing file.
Open the output path with encoding='utf-8' and read its full text.

plans.expected_invariant: Appending trace output to an existing path preserves the non-ASCII value 'naïve' as Unicode text while retaining the pre-existing ASCII prefix.

observable.measurement_point: after the decorated function returns and the append-mode trace file is closed
observable.extraction_method: read the file at the requested path using open(path, encoding='utf-8') and search for the substring 'naïve'

assertion.predicate: The UTF-8 decoded appended trace file contains the exact substring 'naïve' and still starts with 'lala'.
assertion.failure_condition: The substring 'naïve' is absent, or reading the file as UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError, or the decorated call raised UnicodeEncodeError, or the pre-existing 'lala' prefix was lost.
assertion.rationale: The append branch of FileWriter.write also opens the path without encoding='utf-8'; under an ASCII locale the non-ASCII repr cannot be appended correctly, so the exact Unicode value will be missing or the write will fail.

actions.description: Set LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 in the process environment before importing pysnooper.
Create a temporary directory and choose a non-existent output path tmpdir/overwrite_trace.log.
Import pysnooper and define a function decorated with @pysnooper.snoop(path, overwrite=True) that assigns a local variable to the non-ASCII string '日本語'.
Call the decorated function twice so the tracer writes trace lines containing the repr of the non-ASCII local variable to the path, with the second call overwriting the first.
Open the output path with encoding='utf-8' and read its full text.

plans.expected_invariant: Overwriting trace output at the requested path preserves the non-ASCII value '日本語' as Unicode text.

observable.measurement_point: after the second decorated function call returns and the overwrite-mode trace file is closed
observable.extraction_method: read the file at the requested path using open(path, encoding='utf-8') and search for the substring '日本語'

assertion.predicate: The UTF-8 decoded overwritten trace file contains the exact substring '日本語'.
assertion.failure_condition: The substring '日本語' is absent, or reading the file as UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError, or either decorated call raised UnicodeEncodeError.
assertion.rationale: The overwrite branch of FileWriter.write opens the path with mode 'w' and no encoding argument; under an ASCII locale the non-ASCII repr cannot be written correctly, so the exact Unicode value will be missing or the write will fail.
